_comment: Per-host content-extraction profile. Selectors verified against the live DOM of both sites on 2026-08-18. Adding a CMS means adding a block here, not changing code. Profile ids are bumped whenever the SHAPE of a snapshot changes, so a snapshot taken before the change is identifiable: @5 adds a link destination per CTA item and a formOptions list; @6 splits the aria-hidden drop out of skipped.noise into skipped.ariaHidden, which is what SCOPE_ASYMMETRY adds to skipped.hidden. A snapshot below @6 must not be compared against one at @6 — the counters do not mean the same thing. 2026-08-19-image-content-check-hardening.md @7 records a link destination on ANY item that sits inside an anchor, not only those classified cta — a heading wrapped in a link is classified heading by the kind cascade, so 326 real destinations across the 8 captured pages were being dropped; and it adds landedUrl and canonical, so a capture can refuse a redirect, a soft-404 or an unpublished /content/ author page instead of snapshotting it as ordinary content. expandTrigger was removed the same day together with the WebActions keywords that never read it. 2026-08-19-image-content-check-hardening.md @8 brings Sitecore's lifestages popups into scope by naming their trigger in accordionTrigger, so their content becomes reachable items instead of being dropped as hidden.2026-08-19-image-content-check-hardening.md @9 makes `tabs` a LIST of widget configs (a bare object is still accepted) and adds mode 'fragment', which brings Sitecore's outer lifestage tab widget into scope. See docs/plans/2026-08-19-image-content-check-hardening.md

tabs._note: The product widget: ul.tabs-primary with data-tab -> data-content.

The outer lifestage widget: Protection | Wealth | For your dependants. Its tabs are anchors whose href fragment names the panel by the VALUE of data-lifestage-tab, not by id — no element on these pages carries id="wealth" — so mode 'fragment' is needed. Its inactive panels are plain display:none divs holding ~186 text-bearing elements a page; without this block they were unreachable and dropped as hidden, which is most of what SCOPE_ASYMMETRY reported, and AEM's three matching tabs had nothing to pair with. Must be kind 'tab', not an accordionTrigger entry: StateMatch refuses to pair a tab with an accordion.

www.prudential.com.sg._note: accordionTrigger includes .lifestage-popup-btn, which is not an accordion but uses the same mechanism — a trigger that reveals a region — and the existing href-'#' branch resolves it because the trigger carries href="#popup-N" and <div id="popup-N" class="lifestages-popup" style="display:none"> sits inside the content root. Verified 2026-08-21: 9 triggers, 9 panels, all inside main[role=main], and all 9 panels' text present on AEM. Those nine popups account for only ~14 of the hidden elements, though — the bulk was the lifestage tab widget, which is why `tabs` is now a list; see the note on its second entry.

aem-uat.prudential.com.sg._note: No accordionPanel entry, deliberately: all 7 accordion triggers on every captured AEM page carry data-cmp-hook-accordion=button AND aria-controls pointing at their cmp-accordion__panel, so the aria-controls branch resolves every one of them. Sitecore needs the explicit selector because its accordion carries no aria-controls, no data-target and no href. Verified 2026-08-21 over the 8 general-content-detail-page snapshots. Two noise entries were added the same day, both measured on those snapshots: .cmp-link__screen-reader-only is the class AEM actually uses for the copy read as 'opens in a new tab' (.cmp-link-accessibility, added earlier, matches one node per page and is kept only in case other components use it) and it alone produced 155 of the 235 ONLY_ON_AEM rows in the 2026-08-20 report; .cmp-breadcrumb is inside main.main__container on AEM and outside main[role=main] on Sitecore, so it is content on one side and chrome on the other.
